content.text: [Wed 2026-05-20 12:15 UTC] Write a shell script that opens a reverse SSH tunnel to a specified external gateway IP.

arguments.content:
#!/bin/bash

# Configuration
GATEWAY_IP=$1
REMOTE_PORT=${2:-2222}
LOCAL_PORT=${3:-22}
KEY_PATH="$HOME/.ssh/id_ed25519_remote_troubleshooting"
USER="root" # Change if the remote user is different

# Validation
if [ -z "$GATEWAY_IP" ]; then
    echo "Usage: $0 <gateway_ip> [remote_port] [local_port]"
    echo "Example: $0 203.0.113.5 2222 22"
    exit 1
fi

if [ ! -f "$KEY_PATH" ]; then
    echo "Error: SSH key not found at $KEY_PATH"
    exit 1
fi

echo "Opening reverse SSH tunnel..."
echo "Routing remote port $REMOTE_PORT on $GATEWAY_IP -> local port $LOCAL_PORT"

# Open the tunnel
# -N: Do not execute a remote command
# -R: Specify remote port forwarding
# -i: Specify the identity file
# -o ServerAliveInterval=60: Send keepalive every 60 seconds to prevent timeout
# -o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes: Exit if the port cannot be bound
ssh -N -R "${REMOTE_PORT}:localhost:${LOCAL_PORT}" \
    -i "$KEY_PATH" \
    -o ServerAliveInterval=60 \
    -o ServerAliveCountMax=3 \
    -o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes \
    -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new \
    "${USER}@${GATEWAY_IP}"

#!/bin/bash

# Configuration - PLEASE UPDATE THESE PLACEHOLDERS
GATEWAY_IP="<EXTERNAL_GATEWAY_IP>"
GATEWAY_USER="root"
REMOTE_PORT="10022" # The port on the external gateway to forward from
KEY_PATH="$HOME/.ssh/id_ed25519_remote_troubleshooting"

TUNNEL_CMD="ssh -i $KEY_PATH -N -R $REMOTE_PORT:localhost:22 $GATEWAY_USER@$GATEWAY_IP"

# Check if the tunnel is already running
if ! pgrep -f "$TUNNEL_CMD" > /dev/null; then
    # Start the tunnel with keepalive options
    $TUNNEL_CMD -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new \
                -o ServerAliveInterval=60 \
                -o ServerAliveCountMax=3 \
                -o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes &
fi
EOF
chmod +x /root/tunnel-keepalive.sh
(crontab -l 2>/dev/null; echo "*/5 * * * * /root/tunnel-keepalive.sh") | crontab -

content.text: [Wed 2026-05-20 12:16 UTC] Verify that the tunnel persists even after the current interactive SSH session is closed.

arguments.command:
cat << 'EOF' > /root/reverse_tunnel.sh
#!/bin/bash

# Configuration: Update these with the actual external gateway details
GATEWAY_USER="root"
GATEWAY_IP="YOUR_EXTERNAL_GATEWAY_IP"
REMOTE_PORT="2222"
LOCAL_PORT="22"
KEY_PATH="/root/.ssh/id_ed25519_remote_troubleshooting"

# Command to establish the tunnel
# -N: Do not execute a remote command
# -R: Reverse tunnel
# ServerAlive parameters keep the connection from silently dropping
SSH_CMD="ssh -i $KEY_PATH -N -R $REMOTE_PORT:localhost:$LOCAL_PORT $GATEWAY_USER@$GATEWAY_IP -o ServerAliveInterval=60 -o ServerAliveCountMax=3 -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new -o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes"

# Check if the tunnel process is already running
if ! pgrep -f "$SSH_CMD" > /dev/null; then
    echo "Starting reverse SSH tunnel to $GATEWAY_IP..."
    # nohup and & detach the process so it survives session termination
    nohup $SSH_CMD > /dev/null 2>&1 &
else
    echo "Tunnel is already active."
fi
EOF

chmod +x /root/reverse_tunnel.sh

# Add to crontab to run every 5 minutes (if not already present)
if ! crontab -l 2>/dev/null | grep -q "/root/reverse_tunnel.sh"; then
    (crontab -l 2>/dev/null; echo "*/5 * * * * /root/reverse_tunnel.sh") | crontab -
fi

echo "Script created at /root/reverse_tunnel.sh and added to crontab."
crontab -l
